findings.title: Hunter clears its risk window after every sample
findings.evidence: Lines 59-65 append one sample then evaluate the buffer; both branches clear it at 68/72. CTRE computes a percentile over the supplied list.
findings.trigger: Call scan_and_reconcile repeatedly on a new hunter.
findings.impact: The advertised recent window never exceeds one observation; tail risk over the inference window is not measured.

findings.title: Hunter reports on-chain commits without submitting transactions
findings.evidence: The commit branch only increments executed_txs, clears a list and returns "Exergy injected on-chain"; the only Web3 operation is get_block at line 35.
findings.trigger: Run the CLI with either a live RPC or no RPC and receive a COMMIT result.
findings.impact: Operators receive fabricated transaction-success telemetry; the count records local decisions rather than on-chain effects. No execution bypass is alleged.

findings.title: Formal validation recipe calls a removed Make target
findings.evidence: The recipe invokes make verify_lean; the inspected root Makefile defines test-lean (cd proof/lean && lake build) and no verify_lean target.
findings.trigger: Follow step 3 of the documented end-to-end demonstration.
findings.impact: The formal validation step stops with a missing target instead of producing the promised Lean validation.

findings.title: Entropy gate labels agreement as safe without checking correctness
findings.evidence: cluster_samples groups identical nonempty texts together; H is then zero. Lines 80-94 label that result safe and return True; no correctness or evidence predicate exists. Line 152 additionally claims isolated memory and guaranteed fail-stop from repeated string fixtures.
findings.trigger: Supply two or more identical false or unsafe answers.
findings.impact: The PoC accepts the samples and prints a safe-transition verdict even though it has only measured lexical agreement. These verdicts cannot establish hallucination blocking or isolation.

findings.title: Swing formula does not implement its declared triplet ratio
findings.evidence: At swing_pct=66.7 the code computes int((16.7/50)*(120*0.667))=26 ticks; a 240-tick sixteenth pair at 66.7 percent places the second note near tick 160, requiring about 40 ticks offset.
findings.trigger: Choose 66.7 percent swing (the source explicitly calls this pure triplet swing).
findings.impact: Generated offbeat timing is about 146 rather than 160 ticks, so the supplied swing percentage and stated triplet behavior disagree.
